answers.rationale: The 7:15 a.m. Monday setup and hotel-shipped calibration kits make the short, reliable campus transfer decisive. The history supports prioritizing proximity and material handling for schedule-sensitive work days, while not establishing an unconditional preference for the closest hotel in every trip context.

An attached hotel is justified for the early badge pickup, booth logistics, cartons, and late Thursday teardown; any Friday social stay should be treated separately. This is a schedule-specific work-versus-leisure split, not a fixed preference for official blocks, since Erin has also selected independent hotels when commute and agenda risk were manageable.

The independent suite is cheaper after fees, directly across from sessions, cancellable, and better suited to the spouse extension. With a 10:00 a.m. start and no booth or teardown burden, there is no operational reason to accept a longer official-block shuttle. The history shows contextual evaluation of block value rather than a fixed pro- or anti-block rule.

The connected block best protects the 7:00 a.m. breakfasts, late receptions, and Tuesday-Thursday congress obligations, while Fells Point is a better fit once the leisure portion begins Friday. This mirrors prior work-weekend splits but remains agenda-driven rather than evidence of a fixed always-split or always-block lodging preference.
